title: Cross-directory role TTL vs session-extension mismatch causing permission flapping
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
Several customers reported intermittent 'permission denied' errors immediately after role renewals or session extension events, while other accounts showed over-permissioned access for bridged identities. Investigation shows the problem emerges when a user's SAML-linked directory role TTL expires in the source directory but a linked session proxy (cross-directory link) extends the session without synchronizing the role TTL, producing short windows where the enforcement layer receives conflicting role enumerations. This causes either transient denial of access (policy enforcement picks stale deny-first snapshot) or unexpected permission inheritance (duplicate role edges applied twice across directories).

Impact:
- Affects customers using multi-directory SSO mapping + RBAC v2 (approx. 3 known enterprise customers, multiple affected users).
- Errors surface in API calls that require admin-level checks and in console UI feature flags that rely on role snapshots.
- Audit logs show gaps: the audit plane records the session extension event and the directory TTL expiry separately but lacks a correlated reconciliation entry.

Why this ticket:
- Fix the enforcement logic to deterministically reconcile role TTLs and session extensions across linked directories, add tighter audit entries to explain transitions, and ship a short-term mitigation to reduce customer impact while we roll a robust reconciliation for RBAC v2.
repro_steps:
1) Configure two directories (A and B) linked to the same user via SAML linked_id with role mirroring enabled.
2) In directory A assign a short-lived admin role (TTL 60s).
3) Have a session proxy in directory B perform a session-extension call around T+55s.
4) Observe: some enforcement nodes evaluate policies using the expired role snapshot from A while session token remains active due to B's extension.
5) Repeat across different regions/timezones to increase race likelihood.

Observed: permission denied errors for actions requiring the admin role; in other runs, duplication of role edges results in additional permissions being granted until a reconciliation cycle runs.
investigation:
Timeline:
- 2026-03-01: Customer report received via SRE escalation (ticket #CUST-1842).
- 2026-03-02: Reproduced locally in staging with a script that simulates cross-directory extension.
- 2026-03-03: Captured enforcement node logs (node IDs: en-12*, en-13*), saw enforcement decisions using two different role snapshot versions within 2s window.
- 2026-03-04: Confirmed audit plane stores separate events but doesn't correlate 'role_expiry' and 'session_extend' as a single reconciliation candidate.
- 2026-03-05: Hypothesis formed: enforcement cache eviction edge-case + non-atomic role delta application across mirror links.

Key artifacts:
- Repro harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-tests/pull/84 (branch: cross-dir-ttl)
- Enforcement logs (redacted): https://governance.redwood/conflogs/ENFORCE-99321
- Initial RCA doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RBAC/Cross-Directory+TTL+Reconciliation
root_cause: Non-atomic application of role deltas across mirrored directory links combined with an enforcement cache that prioritizes the first-arrived snapshot. When a session extension arrives from a secondary directory, session token state persists but the original directory's role TTL expiry triggers a role delta that is applied asynchronously. Because enforcement caches are per-node and use eventual reconciliation, some nodes evaluate policies with the stale deny-first snapshot while others apply the extended session's grant edges, producing inconsistent decisions. Audit logging records both events separately without a reconciliation tag, making postmortem correlation difficult.
mitigation:
Short-term (customer-facing):
- Deploy a hotfix that treats session-extension events as higher-precedence reconciliation triggers for users with linked directories, forcing immediate role snapshot refresh on enforcement nodes for 5 minutes after extension. Rollout incremental: staging -> canary (10% customers) -> 50% -> 100% within 24 hours.

Workaround advice for customers:
- Avoid very short TTLs on mirrored roles (recommend >= 300s) until patch is live.
- If customers observe 'permission denied' on critical flows, ask SRE to trigger a manual role sync for the affected user (internal endpoint /admin/role-sync).
fix_proposal:
1) Make role-delta application atomic across mirror links: introduce a reconciliation token that is attached to role_delta events; enforcement nodes must fetch role deltas tagged with the token and apply them in a single transaction.
2) Add a 'reconciliation' audit event type that references both role_expiry and session_extend event IDs to make post-facto correlation trivial.
3) Update enforcement cache eviction policy to delay eviction for active sessions with linked-directory flags for a configurable grace window.
4) Add e2e tests in CI to simulate cross-directory TTL edge cases and assert eventual consistency within 2s for all nodes.

Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RBAC/Atomic+Role+Delta+Proposal
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (hotfix): immediate patch to treat session-extend as refresh trigger (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% in 24h).
Phase 1 (v1 fix): implement reconciliation token and audit event; land in runtime-1.24 branch; staging validation for 72h, then controlled canary (week 1).
Phase 2 (safety): CI e2e tests, long-running soak in us-west-2 for one week, update documentation and runbook.

Rollback plan: revert hotfix and revert canary route if error rate > 1% or latency increase > 15% on enforcement requests.
qa_criteria:
- Repro harness no longer shows permission flaps in 1000 iterations.
- All enforcement nodes show consistent policy decisions within 2s after session-extension during staged test.
- Audit logs include reconciliation event linking role_expiry and session_extend for test users.
- No CPU or latency regression >10% on enforcement nodes in canary.
- Security review sign-off obtained (security_review_required=true).
